description: Arrow Protocol Confidence Subprofiles Registry. Defines default confidence ceilings and accountability requirements for specific categories of bridges, oracles, APIs, and third-party attestation sources. Referenced by BRG-006 and SEM-015. Subprofiles feed SEM-015 by specifying more precise ceilings for classes of verification actors — they do not replace SEM-015. v1.5.2 supersedes legal_oracle_structured and legal_attestation_panel with structured_legal_attestation and multiple_legal_attestation. Legal authority panels are LEG authority/finality metadata, not confidence subprofiles.
governance: Editor-controlled for v1.x. Registry extension process to be defined in v2.0.

schema_notes.default_confidence_ceiling: Maximum Confidence claimable by events from actors matching this subprofile, absent additional verification documented in the Bridge Registry or event metadata.
schema_notes.requires_accountable_operator: If true, the asserting entity must be identifiable, registered, or otherwise accountable to an external authority.
schema_notes.requires_source_methodology: If true, the method by which the claim was produced must be documented in the event or registry entry.
schema_notes.requires_dispute_or_challenge_path: If true, the verification claim must include or reference a mechanism by which it can be audited, challenged, or disputed.
schema_notes.default_rejection_behavior: Protocol behavior when a claimant matching this subprofile exceeds its ceiling. Values: reject | downgrade | defer_to_policy

entries.name: Native Canonical Chain
entries.description: Full-node or light-client verified canonical chain state. Proof is native to the chain's own consensus mechanism. No external verifier is required.
entries.notes: Highest-trust subprofile. Classification binding is native because the chain's own state machine enforces type. No override needed.

entries.name: Optimistic Rollup — Settled
entries.description: L2 rollup that has posted state root to L1 and the fraud-proof challenge window has elapsed. Post-settlement confidence is equivalent to L1 canonical.
entries.notes: Pre-settlement optimistic rollup events fall under optimistic_rollup_pre_settlement subprofile (max B). This subprofile covers only post-challenge-window finalized state.

entries.name: Optimistic Rollup — Pre-Settlement
entries.description: L2 rollup that has submitted a state root to L1 but the fraud-proof challenge window has not yet elapsed.
entries.notes: Challenge window is the dispute path. Once the window closes without a successful fraud proof, the subprofile upgrades to optimistic_rollup_settled.

entries.name: Bonded Quorum Bridge
entries.description: Cross-chain bridge relying on M-of-N bonded committee attestation. Quorum signers attest to content. Source-chain output type classification is not typically part of the attested claim unless explicitly documented in the Bridge Registry entry.
entries.notes: Classification binding defaults to false. A deployment may override to true in the Bridge Registry entry if the quorum attestation scheme explicitly attests to source-chain output type — must be documented with classification_audit_ref.

entries.name: Native Notarized Consensus
entries.description: Cross-chain bridge relying on the source chain's own native notarization mechanism, where notarization is part of the source chain's consensus protocol and does not depend on an external destination-side bridge contract. Distinct from bonded_quorum_bridge because the trust basis is the source chain's own consensus, not an external committee.
entries.notes: Introduced to address the native-notarized cross-chain proof case. Verus PBaaS-style native notarization does not fit cleanly into bonded_quorum (no external committee) or native_canonical (destination-side enforcement is still external). Classification binding defaults to false because even with native notarization, destination-side type enforcement depends on the destination bridge contract — which is outside the source chain's consensus boundary.

entries.name: Institutional Custodian
entries.description: Regulated financial institution, licensed custodian, or VASP attesting to events within its custody or operational scope. Attestation is structured, the operator is identifiable and accountable, and challenge paths exist via regulatory or contractual frameworks.
entries.notes: Custodian attests to facts it observes. Output type on a foreign chain is not part of the standard attestation scope and therefore classification_bound defaults to false.

entries.name: Structured Legal Attestation
entries.description: Single accountable legal oracle, Sibyl-style operator, LBRY-style legal record, or equivalent structured legal proof pipeline. The attestation is machine-readable, signed or otherwise accountable, and anchored to source legal evidence.
examples: Structured court-order proof with source-document hash
Signed legal oracle attestation with anchoring transaction
entries.notes: B is the ceiling, not the default. The event still needs sufficient artifacts, a registered or accountable operator, a documented source methodology, and a dispute or audit path. A court, arbitral, or appellate panel belongs to the legal_authority_panel authority/finality axis and does not itself establish this confidence subprofile.

entries.name: Multiple Legal Attestation
entries.description: Independent multi-Sibyl or multi-legal-oracle corroboration of the same legal fact. Independence must be shown at the operator, source, and methodology level.
examples: Two or more independent Sibyl attestations to the same court order
Independent structured legal records anchored by separate operators
entries.notes: Current ceiling is B. This may graduate later only if a future specification defines the operational, cryptographic, and governance conditions under which independent multi-Sibyl evidence reaches A.

entries.name: API — Audited Feed
entries.description: Third-party data feed, oracle, or API provider that operates under a documented methodology, is registered or licensed, and provides a challenge or dispute path for incorrect data. Provider identity is accountable.
examples: Chainlink data feed (audited, registered node operator)
entries.notes: An audited feed has structure, accountability, and reproducibility. It reaches C but not B absent cryptographic settlement, bonded stake, or panel corroboration.

entries.name: API — Raw / Unaccountable
entries.description: Raw API, scraper, unaudited feed, anonymous oracle, or observation source without documented methodology, accountable operator, or challenge path. Suitable for awareness and monitoring only.
entries.notes: D ceiling is firm. Not suitable for high-consequence execution without additional verification from a higher-confidence source.
